description: phasekit's machine-readable interface manifest: the environment variables, artifact files and exit codes through which phasekit and any supervisor (an orchestrator, a cron job, a human wrapper) communicate. Hand-authored by the producer; pinned from both directions by tests/test_interface_manifest.py. Refreshing this file is part of acceptance for any change that touches the interface (docs/CONTRACTS.md, 'Producer responsibilities').
standalone_note: Every input here is honoured WHEN SUPPLIED. No supervisor is required: defaults make every script work standalone, and this manifest is equally the contract a stranger's cron job codes against.

scope.covered: scripts/*.sh, scripts/phasekit-contracts.py, and .claude/hooks/*.sh — the shipped runtime surface a supervisor interacts with.
scope.not_covered: Ambient POSIX environment (HOME, PWD, PATH) and the Claude Code harness's own hook payload (HOOK_PAYLOAD via stdin) are not interface knobs and are not declared. install.sh's PHASEKIT_HOME/PHASEKIT_BIN/PHASEKIT_URL/PHASEKIT_REF are the installer's interface, documented in docs/adr/ADR-0002-self-update-channels.md. The orchestrator's own artifacts (e.g. iteration-mode.json, written and read entirely supervisor-side) are the supervisor's interface, not phasekit's; their phasekit-side reflection is the env family below (e.g. PHASEKIT_ITERATION_MODE).

env.name: PHASEKIT_SESSION_DEADLINE
env.semantics: Epoch seconds of the supervisor's hard kill (the supervisor computes it as start + its MAX_MINUTES); the loop refuses to start an iteration it cannot finish before it and wraps up instead. Non-numeric values are warned about and ignored.

env.name: PHASEKIT_WRAPUP_SENTINEL
env.semantics: Path of the supervisor's soft-stop sentinel file. Existence-only signal: the loop clears a stale one at start, polls between iterations, and finishes with a wrap-up commit when it appears; the wrapup-nudge PostToolUse hook additionally surfaces it to the model MID-iteration, once, so a turn spanning the deadline hears about it before the kill. The default lives inside the workspace, so a containerized supervisor signals by writing the file, not by forwarding this variable; an overrider owns keeping a custom path out of git status.

env.name: PHASEKIT_ITERATION_MODE
env.semantics: standard | light. light is the reduced-ceremony loop for small triaged tasks (caps 2/2, no strategy-planner/red-team, escalate-not-grind); it silently downgrades to standard when the verify gate is absent or still the stub.

env.name: PHASEKIT_ITER_RETRY
env.semantics: Per-iteration retry budget for a non-zero claude CLI exit (transient API/CLI failures). 0 disables retries; after the budget is spent the child's exit code propagates verbatim.

env.name: PHASEKIT_PACING_FLOOR_SECONDS
env.semantics: Minimum remaining-time threshold for deadline pacing; no new iteration starts when less than max(this, 1.2 x average pass duration) remains before PHASEKIT_SESSION_DEADLINE. Non-numeric values fall back to the default.

env.name: PHASEKIT_VERIFY_CMD
env.default: unset — the loop runs scripts/phasekit-verify.sh if present
env.semantics: One-shot shell command overriding the project's verify gate; run via bash -eo pipefail -c. Non-empty also satisfies light-mode verify eligibility on its own.

env.name: PHASEKIT_VERIFY_BUDGET_SECONDS
env.semantics: Seconds above which one verify run counts as over budget; after two such runs the loop prints a one-time fail-open advisory suggesting a fast tier. Non-numeric values fall back to the default.

env.name: VERIFY_SKIP
env.semantics: 1 bypasses the pre-commit verify gate for a run (the routine hatch for red-TDD commits and docs-only phases) and clears artifacts/phase-verify-failed.json. Deliberately does NOT bypass the contracts gate. Also honoured by the seeded scripts/phasekit-verify.sh templates.

env.name: VERIFY_MAX_ATTEMPTS
env.semantics: Consecutive verify-failure circuit breaker; on reaching it the loop writes artifacts/phase-blocked.json (standard) or escalates via artifacts/light-escalation.json (light) and stops with exit 2.

env.name: PHASEKIT_CONTRACTS_SKIP
env.default: unset — contracts gate runs when contracts.yaml declares dependencies
env.semantics: 1 is the loud, operator-only, one-run bypass of the cross-project contracts gate (docs/CONTRACTS.md). Never a committed setting; checked before the missing-checker refusal so it also wins there.

env.name: PHASEKIT_CONTRACTS_MOUNT
env.default: unset — no contracts provider (the normal standalone case)
env.semantics: HOST path to a provider's contracts tree (index.json + one directory per slug). Bind-mounted read-only at /contracts inside the container, announced inward as PHASEKIT_CONTRACTS_DIR=/contracts. Set-but-unusable (not a directory, or no readable index.json) is a hard exit 1, never a silent drop.

env.name: PHASEKIT_CONTRACTS_DIR
env.semantics: Where the provider's contracts tree is readable, consumed by the contracts checker. Set by container-setup.sh when PHASEKIT_CONTRACTS_MOUNT is given; a standalone user sets it by hand to run the gate outside a container.

env.name: PHASEKIT_NO_UPDATE_CHECK
env.semantics: 1 skips the once-per-run, non-fatal upstream release-tag nudge (git ls-remote against the manifest's origin_url).

env.name: PHASEKIT_TRACE
env.semantics: 1 enables bash set -x in the wrapper scripts; container-setup.sh forwards any non-empty value into the container so in-container scripts trace too.

env.name: PHASEKIT_CONTAINER_NAME
env.default: unset — docker assigns a random name
env.semantics: Deterministic docker --name so an outer supervisor can docker kill the container on session timeout.

env.name: PHASEKIT_CONTAINER_USER
env.semantics: Raw docker run --user spec; root normalizes to 0:0 (with HOME=/home/node pinned and IS_SANDBOX=1 exported). Takes precedence over PHASEKIT_ROOTLESS_DOCKER.

env.name: PHASEKIT_ROOTLESS_DOCKER
env.semantics: 1 (with PHASEKIT_CONTAINER_USER empty) runs the container as root, the UID-0 mode for rootless Docker where container root maps to the unprivileged host user.

env.name: PHASEKIT_PYTHON
env.semantics: Interpreter used to run scripts/enrich-project.py, so a global install can point at an isolated venv (e.g. one that has pyyaml).

env.name: CLAUDE_MODE
env.semantics: new = fresh session (also resets a stale phase-verify-failed.json at kickoff); continue = resume the most recent session (-c). The loop consumes it for iteration 1 and sets it per child invocation thereafter.

env.name: MAX_ITERATIONS
env.semantics: Loop iteration ceiling; exhausting it without completion is exit 3. container-setup.sh forwards it only when set, deliberately leaving the mode-aware default to the loop.

env.name: ANTHROPIC_MODEL
env.semantics: Model for the claude invocation (alias like sonnet or a full claude-* id), passed as --model when non-empty. The light-mode final review deliberately unsets it so the review runs on the default model; the value is also recorded in light-escalation.json.

env.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
env.default: unset — fall back to volume-persisted subscription credentials
env.semantics: Pay-per-token API key, forwarded into the container only when non-empty. Missing both this and volume credentials is a warning, not an error.

env.name: AUTO_PUSH
env.semantics: 1 makes the loop git push after every loop-created commit (iteration and wrap-up); push failure is non-fatal.

env.name: IMAGE_NAME
env.semantics: Docker image tag to build/run.

env.name: CLAUDE_VOLUME
env.semantics: Named Docker volume mounted at /home/node/.claude, holding persisted Claude subscription credentials — one volume is the fleet's shared auth.

env.name: PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_VERSION
env.semantics: Passed as --build-arg at image build time (not a runtime -e).

env.name: SKIP_PLAYWRIGHT_MCP
env.semantics: Non-empty skips Playwright MCP injection by the container entrypoint.

env.name: GIT_USER_NAME
env.semantics: Git author name inside the container.

env.name: GIT_USER_EMAIL
env.semantics: Git author email inside the container.

env.name: GH_TOKEN
env.semantics: GitHub token for HTTPS push / gh CLI, forwarded when set. GITHUB_TOKEN is honoured independently under its own name.

env.name: GITHUB_TOKEN
env.semantics: Alternate name for GH_TOKEN; both are forwarded independently when set.

env.name: SSH_AUTH_SOCK
env.default: unset or not a socket — no agent forwarding
env.semantics: Host ssh-agent socket, bind-mounted into the container and rewritten to /ssh-agent for the child.

env.name: CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT
env.default: empty — no pattern matches, hook allows
env.semantics: Supplied by the Claude Code harness to PreToolUse hooks: the tool-invocation payload, substring-matched (lowercased) against the dangerous-command blocklist.

env.name: PHASEKIT_STOP_BLOCK_LIMIT
env.semantics: Max Stop-hook blocks per iteration before the require-verdict hook steps aside and lets the loop's own no-verdict handling take over. Non-numeric values fall back to the default.

env.name: PHASEKIT_VERDICT_ARTIFACTS
env.semantics: Space-separated verdict-artifact vocabulary, exported by the loop from its VERDICT_ARTIFACTS array (the single source of truth) so the Stop hook and the dispatcher cannot disagree about what an ending is. Not honoured from the outer environment: the loop assigns it unconditionally.

env.name: PHASEKIT_ARTIFACTS_DIR
env.semantics: Absolute path of the repo's artifacts/ directory, exported by the loop for the Stop hook. Not honoured from the outer environment: the loop assigns it unconditionally.

env.name: PHASEKIT_ITER_MARKER
env.semantics: Path of the loop's iteration-start marker file (a mktemp path, touched before every claude invocation); the Stop hook only counts verdict artifacts newer than it.

env.name: PHASEKIT_ITER
env.semantics: Iteration number embedded in the per-iteration log filenames (artifacts/logs/claude-iter-N.*). Set per invocation by the loop; the manual default labels direct run-phase.sh runs.

env.name: PHASEKIT_RETRY_ATTEMPT
env.semantics: Retry ordinal for the current iteration; >0 appends -retryN to log filenames so a retry never overwrites the first attempt's logs.

env.name: IS_SANDBOX
env.semantics: Set to 1 for the container only when running as UID 0, because Claude Code refuses --permission-mode bypassPermissions as root without it.

env.name: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
env.semantics: Unconditionally set for the container so the claude CLI finds the volume-persisted credentials regardless of the effective user.

env.name: PHASEKIT_VERIFY_CONFIGURED
env.semantics: NOT read from the environment: a sentinel LINE inside the project-owned scripts/phasekit-verify.sh. The seeded stub carries PHASEKIT_VERIFY_CONFIGURED=0; a configured gate flips it to 1. The loop greps for it to decide light-mode eligibility, and enrich-project.py uses it to know the stub may be replaced by a stack template on upgrade.

env.name: PHASEKIT_CHANNEL_DEFAULT
env.semantics: Library constant (unconditional assignment when sourced), not an input knob: the channel used when a scaffold checkout has no .phasekit-channel file. Setting it in the environment has no effect.

env.name: PHASEKIT_CANONICAL_ORIGIN
env.semantics: Internal constant: the fallback upstream URL for the release-tag nudge when the manifest carries no origin_url. Setting it in the environment has no effect.

env.name: PHASEKIT_LEARNINGS_WARN_KB
env.semantics: Advisory-only threshold in KB for the once-per-session docs/LEARNINGS.md size note. At or over the threshold the loop prints one stderr line suggesting a curation pass per the file's own header rule; it never blocks, never rotates, and never alters prompts (the doc-rotation descope, 2026-08-20). Non-numeric values disable the check. Supervisors that want scheduling watch the same file size themselves.

artifacts.name: phase-approval.json
artifacts.lifecycle: durable — committed with the phase, deliberately never deleted by iteration cleanup
artifacts.when: Written by the Claude session at the end of a phase to approve it; the loop commits it (freshness-gated against the iteration-start marker).

artifacts.name: phase-update.json
artifacts.lifecycle: committed when produced, deleted at each iteration start
artifacts.when: Written by the session when it revised the phase plan/roadmap instead of approving a phase; the loop commits it.

artifacts.name: project-complete.json
artifacts.lifecycle: durable — committed as the project's completion record; deleted at each iteration start until real
artifacts.when: Written by the session when every phase is approved and acceptance criteria are met; in light mode it must survive an adversarial final review to count. Its presence after the final commit is the loop's exit-0 signal.

artifacts.name: phase-blocked.json
artifacts.lifecycle: transient signal — deleted at each iteration start; kept out of commits but deliberately visible in git status
artifacts.when: Written by the session when it needs external input, or by the loop itself when VERIFY_MAX_ATTEMPTS consecutive verify failures trip the circuit breaker. Either way the loop stops with exit 2.

artifacts.name: phase-verify-failed.json
artifacts.lifecycle: transient signal — cleared on verify pass, on VERIFY_SKIP, or at a fresh CLAUDE_MODE=new kickoff; NOT a verdict (the session is still expected to answer); visible in git status
artifacts.when: Written by the loop after each failed verify (or contracts-gate) run, carrying the failure for the next iteration to fix. attempts feeds the circuit breaker.

artifacts.name: session-handoff.json
artifacts.lifecycle: durable across the boundary — committed with the wrap-up; the NEXT session's continue prompt reads then deletes it
artifacts.when: Written by the loop on wrap-up paths (sentinel honoured or deadline pacing) as the baton for the next session.

artifacts.name: ready-to-deploy.json
artifacts.lifecycle: durable — committed inside the iteration's work
artifacts.when: Written by the session when the project is ready for a deploy; phasekit's scripts neither read nor write it — the vocabulary is defined by phasekit's workflow docs (docs/QUALITY_GATES.md) and the file is the supervisor's deploy trigger.

artifacts.name: scope-refusal.json
artifacts.lifecycle: transient signal — hidden from git status; consumed from disk by the supervisor
artifacts.when: Written by the loop's commit gate when a light-mode iteration staged scaffold-class files it may not touch; the commit is refused and light mode escalates (exit 2).

artifacts.name: light-escalation.json
artifacts.lifecycle: transient signal — hidden from git status; consumed from disk by the supervisor
artifacts.when: Written by the loop when a light-mode run needs promotion to a standard iteration (scope refusal, repeated verify failure, review withdrawal, or the iteration cap). Accompanies exit 2 (or exit 3 for the cap).

artifacts.name: scope-warning.json
artifacts.lifecycle: transient signal — hidden from git status; advisory only
artifacts.when: Written by the loop's commit gate when a standard-mode commit touches scaffold-class files — allowed, but flagged for the operator.

artifacts.name: spec-change.json
artifacts.lifecycle: transient signal — hidden from git status; read-then-deleted by the supervisor
artifacts.when: Written by the loop's commit gate when docs/SPEC.md is part of the staged change, so a supervisor can surface spec drift.

artifacts.name: wrapup-requested
artifacts.lifecycle: sentinel — existence-only, contents never read; cleared stale at loop start, removed once honoured; excluded from git status
artifacts.when: Written by the outer supervisor at T-minus-N to request a soft stop; the loop finishes the current iteration, wrap-up commits, and exits 0.

artifacts.name: mutation-run.json
artifacts.lifecycle: audit record of an opt-in mutation-testing run (with-mutation profile only)
artifacts.when: Written by the opt-in mutation harness when a session runs the mutation protocol; see docs/MUTATION_TESTING.md.

artifacts.name: logs
artifacts.lifecycle: internal — never committed (the loop unstages artifacts/logs on every commit path) and excluded from git status
artifacts.when: claude-iter-N[-retryM].jsonl (raw stream-json + stderr) and .log (rendered via phasekit-log-fmt.sh) per claude invocation.

artifacts.name: .scope-check.tmp
artifacts.lifecycle: internal staging file for the scope check; promoted to scope-warning.json or removed within one gate run; hidden from git status
artifacts.when: Exists only inside post_verify_commit_gates. Do not rely on it.

artifacts.name: .wrapup-nudge-sent
artifacts.lifecycle: internal once-per-iteration marker (empty file); freshness against the iteration marker decides, and iteration cleanup deletes it beside .stop-hook-blocks; hidden from git status
artifacts.when: The wrapup-nudge hook's once-per-iteration bookkeeping. Do not rely on it.

artifacts.name: session-interrupted.json
artifacts.lifecycle: dead-man baton: written at every iteration start, deleted by the loop's EXIT trap when the iteration concludes with a verdict; one that survives to the NEXT session's start is promoted to session-handoff.json (unless a real wrap-up baton exists, which wins) and consumed by the orientation there. Same six keys as session-handoff.json. Never committed; hidden from git status
artifacts.when: The previous session was killed or exited without concluding its iteration. Read via its promotion to session-handoff.json, not directly.

artifacts.name: .stop-hook-blocks
artifacts.lifecycle: internal per-iteration counter (plain integer, not JSON); deleted by iteration cleanup so the block budget resets; hidden from git status
artifacts.when: The Stop hook's bounded-block bookkeeping. Do not rely on it.

conventions.name: spec-acceptance-criteria-append-only
conventions.semantics: The SPEC's acceptance-criteria section is append-only: sessions add criteria and supersede them (prefix the old line with the marker, exactly, followed by the replacement criterion's number and a colon-space; full replacement text lives in the appended criterion), and never delete or renumber. Removals only via operator change-request. The marker literal is the cross-repo contract a supervisor's spec-change detector keys on: a removal or rewrite of an existing criterion line without it is a high-confidence violation; append-only changes auto-clear.

conventions.name: approval-deferrals
conventions.semantics: Verdict artifacts (phase-approval.json, project-complete.json) may carry a top-level 'deferrals' array of {item, reason, suggested_task} objects plus an optional 'key', one entry per in-scope acceptance item the session deliberately did not implement. 'item' MUST name the AC number when the deferral maps to a criterion. 'key' is the stable dedupe identifier: it defaults to that AC number (e.g. 'AC#3') when 'item' cites one, and MUST be supplied explicitly (kebab-case) otherwise; entries with the same key across artifact rewrites or successive approvals are the SAME deferral and are never refiled. The supervisor files one queue task per new key so deferred scope cannot lose its slot — and those tasks land HELD (ops lane or approval-gated), never pre-approved: a session's own deferral entry is not self-granted authorization for follow-up work. Absence of the field claims everything in scope shipped; a deferral recorded only in prose is a violation of the deferred-scope gate — this field is the sole machine-readable home.

conventions.name: blocked-reason-review-nonconvergence
conventions.semantics: The exact 'reason' literal a session writes into artifacts/phase-blocked.json when the review-fix convergence gate trips (two consecutive fix rounds each introduced new MAJOR findings). Sessions must use the literal verbatim; a supervisor branching on blocked-reason may key on it to route non-convergence to an operator or redesign lane rather than a generic stall path.

codes.0: finished cleanly: project completion committed, wrap-up sentinel honoured, deadline pacing wrapped up, or stranded work recovered with nothing left to do
codes.1: loop-owned failure: a required command (jq, git) is missing, or the session ended with NO verdict artifact and the loop cannot dispatch (the silence failure the Stop hook exists to prevent)
codes.2: stopped, external input required: phase-blocked.json present, a commit was blocked, or a light-mode run escalated
codes.3: MAX_ITERATIONS reached without project completion (light mode also writes light-escalation.json with trigger iteration_cap)

scripts/run-until-done.sh.passthrough: Any other code is the claude CLI's own exit, propagated verbatim after the PHASEKIT_ITER_RETRY budget is exhausted — including 124 from a supervisor-side timeout and 137 from SIGKILL. The loop assigns meaning only to 0/1/2/3.

codes.1: usage error: no prompt-file argument, or the prompt file does not exist

scripts/run-phase.sh.passthrough: Otherwise the claude CLI's exit status, unmodified (pipefail); nothing is remapped.

codes.0: nothing declared, or every declared contract byte-matches the provider (also all status/provider/refresh success paths)
codes.2: malformed declaration or provider manifest (also missing pyyaml, and CLI usage errors)
codes.3: unobtainable: no provider mounted, or the provider does not offer a declared slug; refreshing cannot help
codes.4: drift: the vendored copy is missing or differs from the mounted one; fix is the named refresh command
codes.5: unverifiable: contracts.yaml exists but scripts/phasekit-contracts.py does not (scaffold predates v0.7.0). Emitted by the LOOP into phase-verify-failed.json, never by the checker itself; fix is phasekit upgrade

codes.1: precondition/config failure: docker missing, PHASEKIT_CONTRACTS_MOUNT unusable (not a directory, or no readable index.json), or an unknown command

scripts/container-setup.sh.passthrough: Otherwise docker build's or the in-container process's exit status verbatim — so run-until-done.sh's codes surface unchanged, as do docker's own conventions (125/126/127, 137 for docker kill).

codes.0: all executed checks passed (skipped checks count as neither)
codes.1: at least one check failed (aggregate; see the FAIL lines on stdout for which)

codes.0: success (check-version is informational and returns 0 even when behind)
codes.1: usage or I/O failure (missing target, unreadable manifest, non-canonical checkout for channel/self-update)
codes.2: lock contention — another enrich-project.py holds the target's lock
codes.3: drift detected by the check verb (DRIFT / MISSING / TEMPLATE DRIFT)

scripts/phasekit.sh.passthrough: The CLI execs scripts/enrich-project.py, so these are the engine's codes; a missing PHASEKIT_PYTHON interpreter surfaces as the shell's 126/127.

codes.0: allow the stop: hook inert (loop env absent), a fresh verdict artifact exists, the block budget is spent, or the counter is unwritable (cannot bound, so must not block)
codes.2: block the stop (Stop-hook contract): no verdict artifact newer than the iteration marker; bounded to PHASEKIT_STOP_BLOCK_LIMIT blocks per iteration

codes.0: no blocklist pattern matched (including an empty payload — fail-open)
codes.2: deny the tool call (PreToolUse hook contract): a dangerous pattern matched

codes.0: always — contractually fail-open; internal python failures are swallowed and output is capped at 2048 bytes

conventions.124: reserved for 'killed by an outer timeout wrapper'. No phasekit script ever exits 124 deliberately, so a supervisor may treat it as its own timeout reflected back.
conventions.137: SIGKILL (e.g. docker kill by a supervisor on hard deadline), propagated verbatim.
conventions.note: A wrapper distinguishing 'loop verdict' from 'child failure' relies on run-until-done.sh owning exactly 0/1/2/3 and everything else being passthrough.
